charts.title: Closed-loop co-simulation — pathogen clearance and the controller's live PK
charts.caption: Closed-loop sepsis co-simulation at severity 3 over 2 h (120 s/tick). ONE process-bigraph composite couples the Tellurium sepsis physiology engine to an antibiotic-PK controller process; they exchange state every tick (controller reads the pathogen, integrates a one-compartment PK, writes the drug-killed pathogen back via the engine's parameters_in port). Untreated (controller inert) is the matched control. The loop clears bacteremia — the driver of septic collapse — while the untreated arm's pathogen climbs. The downstream clinical endpoint (MAP < 65 mmHg at ~54 h, tissue integrity 0.24 at 72 h; studies 03/05) is a 2–3 day process not reached at this horizon; this figure shows the controlled variable and the controller's live PK, i.e. the loop removing the cause. The treated arm's sawtooth is the per-tick coupling made visible: the pathogen regrows within each physiology step and the controller knocks it back down at every tick. (At this horizon the untreated arm's tissue integrity has only just begun to fall, ~0.983 vs 1.000 treated — the early edge of the collapse.)

charts.title: Treatment counterfactuals (untreated / early / delayed) + coupling-step convergence
charts.caption: Treatment counterfactuals from the identical sepsis_cosim composite (severity 3, 2 h, delay 1 h). Untreated, early, and delayed treatment differ only in when the controller starts. Early treatment clears bacteremia (final 0.0057); delayed lets it accumulate first (0.16) then clears it; untreated climbs (11). Tissue integrity ends 1.000 early vs 0.983 untreated. The convergence panel runs the early arm at 240/120/60 s per tick: as the coupling step shrinks the final bacteremia changes by 0.0548, so the co-simulation is numerically consistent. This separates execution success (the coupling runs and converges) from pharmacological credibility (the PK is illustrative, not calibrated).
